newsitem.title: UK: London gold dealers brace for fresh price falls.
newsitem.headline: London gold dealers brace for fresh price falls.

text.p: Fresh falls were forecast for precious metals prices after both gold and platinum stumbled along at their lowest levels in over three years, traders said on Friday.
"Historically the first few days of a new year have set the tone for the first quarter, so it looks like weakness is set to continue for the moment," one senior bullion dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $364.30 per ounce compared with $366.55 on Thursday afternoon and a London close of $366.85.
It was its lowest fix since $363.00 on November 3, 1993.
In New York, Comex's February futures contract was off $2.60 at $366.60 on Thursday.

Gold fixed at its all-time highest level of $850 per ounce in January 1980 when rising oil prices and inflation threatened the value of currencies across the western world, but then went into a lengthy decline.

Early last year however, prices soared to their highest levels since before the Gulf War as the investment funds piled into the market. Their buying pushed gold over $416.00 on February 2, its highest price since February 22, 1990, but the rally was brief.
By the end of June, bullion was valued at around $380.00, a level not seen since September 1995 and a slower but inexorable fall in value has continued every since.
Gold's latest price weakness may have been exaggerated by the absence of many traders during the Christmas and New Year holidays, dealers said.
"Physical demand is there but it tends to be "cute' in some places. These people will know to hold off buying for now to see if they can get in at lower prices later," a dealer said.
Some dealers were now looking for gold to probe as low as $360 per ounce, a value not seen since early October 1993.
"After that its a parachute job," one dealer said, adding that the investment fund portfolios were positioned to take advantage of weaker prices.
The fresh fall in gold prices came despite signs on Thursday that U.S. inflation was less benign that was generally believed and fresh falls in stock markets in London and New York.
The U.S. bond and stocks markets slumped on Thursday when a higher-than-expected December National Association of Purchasing Managers index indicated the possibility of higher inflation.

The index rose to 54.0 from 52.7 in November. A reading above 50 indicates an expansion in the manufacturing sector and the possibility of higher inflation but that coupled with falling stock markets failed to direct investment into gold.

"Its not clear that there is enough fresh news in the market to replace the bearish psychology which prevailed before Christmas," said bullion market analyst Tony Warwick-Ching at research group CRU International.
The other precious metals were also lower on Friday. Platinum edged down $2.50 to fix at $366.50 per ounce, its lowest fixing since November 2, 1993 on weak demand.
Silver edged a couple of cents lower with gold to be indicated at $4.70 but palladium remained relatively buoyant at $120.25, down just $0.50.
